company.name: Vessel
company.shortDescription: Vessel is a flexible integration platform for GTM tools, supporting CRMs and sales engagement platforms.
company.description:
Vessel is a developer-first, native integration platform for GTM tools. Integrations are complex and existing solutions are rigid. Choose how you want to integrate with your customer’s tools, quickly and deeply with our solutions fitted for your complex needs.

Support for integrations with CRMs, Marketing Automations, Sales Engagement Platforms, Dialers, and more.

productsAndServices.description: A developer-first platform that enables building customer-facing integrations with various sales, marketing, and CRM tools through unified APIs and real-time data synchronization.
productsAndServices.name: Vessel Integration Platform

productsAndServices.description: Prebuilt native API integrations with popular CRM, sales engagement, marketing, project management, and e-commerce platforms to enable real-time data access and manipulation.
productsAndServices.name: Native Integrations (e.g., ActiveCampaign, Accelo, Apollo, Dropbox, Jira, Mural, Shopify, Square, Workable, Zoho)

productsAndServices.description: A service that handles the extraction and loading of data between customer applications and databases, managing synchronization and data flow.
productsAndServices.name: Managed Data Pipelines

insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $5,564,491 to $5,564,491, a 1x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 66 (+2 over 90 days) and market heat at 23 (+14).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
